risk_if_not_implemented: Without Incident Response Capabilities Testing, security incidents may not be detected, contained, investigated or communicated in a timely manner, increasing their scope, duration and cost. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct tests and/or exercises to evaluate the contingency plan's effectiveness and the organization's readiness to execute the plan.
compensating_control_1.justification: Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises (BCD-10) provides periodic assessment and assurance that compensates for the absence of Incident Response Testing (IRO-09) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Incident Response Training
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to train personnel in their incident response roles and responsibilities.
compensating_control_2.justification: Incident Response Training (IRO-10) provides personnel training and awareness that compensates for the absence of Incident Response Testing (IRO-09) by reducing human-factor risk by equipping personnel to recognize and respond to relevant threats. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
